headline: Affordable coastal district with low density and severe transport connectivity gaps

tags.reason: The affordability index stands at 96 against the Baku median of 50, with estimated secondary apartment prices at 1,452 AZN/m² compared to the city median of 2,084 AZN/m².
Population density is low at 627 residents per km² against the median of 2,890.5, with air quality showing PM2.5 levels of 10.9 compared to the median 12.8.

summary: Pirallahı presents an affordability index score of 96 against the Baku median of 50, alongside estimated secondary apartment prices of 1,452 AZN/m² based on a 50-listing sample where 90% possess title extract documentation ('çıxarış'). Social provision metrics per capita are above typical city medians, showing 6.38 schools and 4.26 hospitals per 10,000 residents compared to medians of 3.43 and 2.75. However, transport connectivity is heavily restricted, marked by a transport index of 8 versus the city median of 55.5 and a distance of 31.3 km to the nearest metro station. Paved road quality is notably low, with only 7.6% of known roads paved compared to the median of 83.1%.
strengths: High housing affordability ranking relative to the city baseline (affordability index 96; median 50)
Extensive park density relative to population size (39.36 parks per 10,000 residents; median 10.04)
Above-average per-capita primary education facility density (6.38 schools per 10,000 residents; median 3.43)
weaknesses: Critically low transport connectivity score (transport index 8; median 55.5)
Minimal share of paved surfaces across recorded roads (7.6% paved; median 83.1%)
Substantial travel distance required to reach rapid transit (nearest metro 31.3 km; median 0 metro stations within district)
best_for: Buyers prioritising lower entry property prices, with secondary flats estimated at 1,452 AZN/m².
Households seeking low-density surroundings, with population density at 627 residents per km².
watch_out: Public transport records only 0.53 bus stops per 10,000 residents (1 stop in total) and 0 mapped bus routes.
Road quality data is missing for 69.6% of the 280 km network, with only 7.6% confirmed as paved.
Mortgage eligibility in local market listings is low at 26% of available adverts.
confidence_note: OpenStreetMap data coverage is medium ('orta'), indicating that a portion of local infrastructure and routes is not yet mapped. New build flat values (1,650 AZN/m²), commercial properties (1,800 AZN/m²), and land plots (8,000 AZN/sot) carry demo values ('mock') and must not be used for transactional conclusions.
